title: Exact nonlinear-complexity distribution of periodic binary sequences
summary: Determine the exact number of binary sequences of every period and every admissible nonlinear complexity, beyond the known high-complexity range.

formal_statement.body: For a positive integer $n$ and an admissible complexity $c$, let $P(n,c)$ be the set of binary $n$-periodic sequences $s$ with $\operatorname{nlc}(s)=c$, where $\operatorname{nlc}$ is the minimum length of an NFSR generating $s$. Determine $|P(n,c)|$ exactly for every pair $(n,c)$, equivalently the complete nonlinear-complexity distribution of binary $n$-periodic sequences.

scope.domain: Periodic binary sequences and nonlinear feedback shift registers
assumptions: Periodicity and sequence equality use the source convention
Nonlinear complexity is the minimum NFSR length
scope.unresolved_remainder: The source gives exact structure and counts when c >= floor(3n/4). A complete exact distribution for lower complexity values, apart from previously settled isolated ranges, remains open.

progress.summary: The source derives exact structure and enumeration for nonlinear complexity at least floor(3n/4) and explicitly leaves the complete distribution open.
